subject: Private hosting — goals, network constraints, and next owners
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting — goals, network constraints, and next owners

Thanks again for a productive call earlier, Beth/Tom — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same runway.

High-level goals you reiterated:
- Data must remain in US (primary tenancy in us-east-1).
- No outbound egress from the inference cluster to third-party internet endpoints (air-gapped or strictly NATed outbound only to approved IPs).
- Strong key management requirement (customer-managed KMS/HSM or bring-your-own HSM).
- SLA target: p95 inference latency <= 200ms for single-turn calls; target throughput ~1k concurrent requests during business hours.
- Auditability: event-level logs retained 365 days and accessible for audits.

Primary pain points we heard:
1) Network ops cannot allow dynamic high-port egress; all outbound must be via a small set of static egress IPs you control.
2) Procurement/legal needs a concrete security artifact bundle (SOC2 evidence, encryption architecture, data flow diagram) to unblock the vendor review.
3) Integration timeline: you'd like a pilot within 8 weeks and a production cutover in 12–14 weeks contingent on procurement.

Technical constraints we called out on our side:
- We can run in a customer VPC with a private control plane model (control plane traffic over a managed, encrypted tunnel).
- Option A (preferred): Dedicated VPC peering + static egress NAT gateway (your-managed).
- Option B: On-premise appliance (air-gapped) for customers requiring fully fenced, offline inference — longer lead time and additional ops support.

Immediate next steps (owners & due dates):
- Redwood: draft schematic network diagram and proposed static IP ranges by EOW (Aditya).
- Cereon: confirm procurement target date and legal reviewer contact (Beth).
- Redwood: prepare SOC2 artifact checklist + short writeup on KMS/HSM options (Neha) — deliver by Tue, Dec 8.
- Joint: 30-minute technical follow-up to validate perf (latency/throughput) assumptions — propose Wed 12/10 or Thu 12/11.

Attachments: network-diagram_v1.pdf (sketch), placeholder tco sheet (we will send a TCO estimate after we confirm architecture).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, call it out. Otherwise we'll treat these as our commitments and follow up on the dates above.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Tessa — thanks, this is very clear and aligns with what we discussed. A handful of clarifications from our side:

- Procurement & legal: our procurement lead (Marta Solis) will need a one-page security summary + SOC2 snapshot and the draft SOW to start internal approvals. Can you provide an early SOW outline or even a scope-of-work bullet list?
- Egress IPs: we can provide a /29 for static egress and will route through our NAT egress appliance. We need HW/port range requirements from you for the firewall rule ticket.
- KMS/HSM: our security team prefers customer-managed keys in our KMS; if there's any required HSM for attestation that adds procurement time, flag that now.
- Pilot scope: toward your suggested pilot, we want the pilot to cover 3 endpoints (payments, notes extraction, and clinical search) and a throughput test that simulates peak-day traffic (we'll share traffic profile next week).

Procurement timeline: we aim to have vendor paperwork in procurement by 12/15 if we have the security summary and draft SOW by 12/8. That matches your dates — thank you.

Can Aditya/Neha start the firewall-ready port list and a one-page security snapshot we can reuse for the procurement packet? I'll loop Marta on Monday.

-Beth

Beth — looped in with a few technical clarifications and an initial artifact list. Thanks for the clear asks.

Firewall / port guidance (initial):
- Outbound: HTTPS (443) to Redwood control-plane endpoints (we will provide static IPs) and outbound to our patch/update endpoints for the inference runtime (if you choose the managed updater). If air-gapped, the appliance requires periodic offline patch bundles.
- Inbound: none required to the inference cluster.
- Egress: we recommend allowing the /29 you mentioned; we'll specify exact IPs in the network diagram update.

KMS options:
- Option 1 (fastest): Redwood uses customer-managed KMS keys in the customer account (we provide IAM role + key policy templates). No separate HSM required unless you need FIPS-level attestation.
- Option 2 (attested HSM): customer provides HSM-attested keys; procurement lead time typically +3–5 weeks.

Artifacts I'll attach as drafts: redwood-vpc-runbook-draft.md (runbook + firewall policy), a short SOC2 snapshot (one-pager) and a rough TCO worksheet — see attachments. I'll refine once we lock the architecture.

Proposed next technical touch: Wed 12/10 10:00–10:30 PT (I can run a short perf/latency assumptions session). Tessa, do you want me to include our runtime engineer (Neha will also join)?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
